defect_observations.observation: No 'toc: P15 170 170.7' tag maps 170.7 (or 170.8, 170.9) to this file. The sibling chapter-170 files carry tags (sequential-evidence-and-multiple-testing-w02b-p15-061.tex line 1: 170.5,170.6; ...-w02b-p15-063.tex line 1: 170.10). The packet's owned file handbook/parts/p15/sequential-evidence-and-multiple-testing-w02b-p15-062.tex does not exist. So only the packet's reader_evidence maps 170.7 to this file, and no heading carries the TOC title 'Hypothesis families and familywise error'. The matching material sits under 'The family, its sampling law and obtained levels' (line 13).

The packet records sources_held=false and held_paths=[] for ED26-METHOD-multiple-testing. Yet held-sources.json lists source/references/p15-multiple-testing/holm-1979-sequentially-rejective.pdf (sha256 4317a0d1...) and holm-1979-extracted.txt (sha256 1c9019d0...). Those two entries have empty titles, bibkeys and source_ids, and null version, extent_verified and body_state. The registry therefore does not by itself tie the files to the selected presentation. This audit established the identity and the complete extent by opening the PDF (physical pp. 2-7 = printed pp. 65-70, Scand. J. Statist. 6(2), 1979) and from acquisition.json, whose URL matches the queue's source_presentations URL.

The ten-normal example is attributed to Holm pp. 67-68. The body reports Bonferroni 0.4412670349 and Holm 0.5631999191 but does not mention that the source prints 0.439 and 0.565 (held txt lines 320-322, printed p. 68), and the difference is not reconciled. Correctness was not assessed.

The protection proof moves from 'a true hypothesis is rejected' to 'the comparison at the smallest true rank j was reached and passed'. It relies on the prefix characterization in the body (lines 94-95) without restating it, and 'that true hypothesis' could mean either the rejected one or the rank-j one. The steps are written and this is not a sketch.

Three source remarks are not reproduced in the treatment. First, Holm claims strictly larger power 'except in trivial non-interesting cases' (printed p. 67). Second, he explains that the gain is small when hypotheses are 'almost true' and considerable when they are 'completely wrong' (printed p. 67). Third, his closing design remark asks for (approximately) independent statistics for design rather than computational reasons (printed p. 70, txt lines 597-610). The handbook instead says the dominance inequalities need not be strict (body line 151). No component success condition requires these remarks.
